title: Wa rusulihi – belief in Allah’s messengers
intro: The fourth pillar of iman: we believe in all of Allah’s messengers.

learn.html: Wa rusulihi means believing in Allah’s messengers. Allah (SWT) chose people to whom He sent revelation. The messengers explained Allah’s guidance to people, called them to good and turned them away from evil.

learn.title: The first and the last
learn.html: Adam (AS) was the first human being and the first prophet. Allah taught him how to live on Earth, and after him sent messengers to people. Muhammad (SAW) is Allah’s last messenger – after him there will be no new messenger and no new revelation.

learn.title: How many messengers?
learn.html: The hadiths mention 124,000 prophets. The Qur’an names 25 of them. The most chosen of them, the ulul-‘azm (those of firm resolve), are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, ‘Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them).

learn.text: The 25 messengers named in the Qur’an

learn.html: Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Ishaq, Isma‘il, Lut, Ya‘qub, Yusuf, Ayyub, Shu‘ayb, Musa, Harun, Dhul-Kifl, Dawud, Sulayman, Ilyas, Al-Yasa‘, Yunus, Zakariyya, Yahya, ‘Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them all).

items.label: Sidq – they always told the truth
Amanah – they were trustworthy, reliable and honest
Tabligh – they passed on Allah’s revelation exactly and completely
‘Ismah – they were kept pure from sin
Fatanah – they were wise and sharp-minded
Muhammad (SAW) – a shepherd, later a trader

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: The messengers lived simply and worked with their hands. When we mention a messenger’s name we say ‘alayhis-salaam (AS) – peace be upon him. Their lives and their manners are an example for every believer.
